author: coordinator

text: Upload-size risk for p. The p model archive is 15.06 GB; submission 1's was 9.21 GB and the September model 8.0 GB, both accepted. Several Grand Challenge challenge pages state a per-upload cap of 10 GB for verified users (2 GB for unverified). The official documentation states no model limit, and a platform admin wrote on the forum that the cap is not checked before the upload, so a refusal may come only after the full upload. The t3 model archive (8.81 GB) is under that cap; t2 (15.04 GB raw) and t1 (19.30 GB raw) are not. Bringing p under 10 GB per file would need either moving about 5.5-6.3 GB of weights into the image (both files would then be about 9.4-10 GB gz, tight, and the image about 14 GB uncompressed against a stated 10 GB container guideline) or more fp16 weight copies (numerics change; needs the packaged-mode parity runs again). I did neither. The Try-out note says: upload p as planned; if the model upload is refused or its import fails, switch both files to t3.

text: For the coordinator's 09:16 EST request (p3 = p2 with ViT-L s46 replaced by the encoder-LR-2e-5 full-data run; p3b = s47 too). Pod only: no transfer, no build, no upload, no Colab run. p, t3 and p2 are only read. Tools are in lane_cellroute_20261109/inference/p3_20261114/. make_p3_20261114.py VARIANT CD_PARAMS MD5 46=NEW [47=NEW] copies the p2 context into package_20261114/<p3|p3b>, refusing an existing folder. It points the named vitl_seeds tta at the new final.pt and adds the new path to fp16_files.txt, so the new weights are read as an fp16 copy like every other regression member (ViT-L final.pt is already on that list). It swaps the model_files.txt line, sets params cd to the deploy block of the CD lane's freeze_cd_params_<V>_20261114.json (md5 checked against the argument, keys equal to p2's, its model_files must name the new path), and updates the Dockerfile header (TIER=<V>, tag <date>-freeze-9687076-<V>) and MANIFEST.json. It writes model_add/<path> (the fp16 copy, sha256 checked) and model_swap.tsv (old path, new path, sha256): the only change to the tier-p model tree. p3b is the same call with the s47 swap added. A dry run on the pod (into /tmp, with p2 constants) produced the expected manifest, params, model_files and Dockerfile diffs. p3_weights_20261114.py does the load test and conversion. It requires complete.json, then compares tensor names, shapes, dtypes and finiteness against the tier-p ViT-L final.pt of the same seed (the old file passes the strict member load, so the new one will too), checks that the weights differ, and writes the fp16 copy with convert_fp16.one() (the 11-11 rule, verified bit for bit; nothing is overwritten). A waiter runs it as soon as the run's complete.json appears. Note on paths: the new arm writes under fold-1, so the s46 path is arms/vitlfu_elr2e5_f99_s46/raw/runs/fold-1/dinov3_l16t/final.pt, the same as in the CD lane's builder (A-CD-0916-P3-BUILDER). Parity: run_parity_p3_20261114.sh <V> uses the p2 harness, frames and settings (fp16b1, switches on, GPU 0/3 with 8 GB) and compares against p2_all with compare_p3_20261114.py: CD and V per frame, CV/HEX maximum difference, differing parts, ViT-L stage seconds, read bytes. It starts when the weights and the CD constants exist. Box: build_test_p3_20261114.sh takes the variant from its folder and runs build, then model (test_model_<V> = hard links to test_model_p minus the old path plus the new file, no copy and no change to test_model_p; per-file sha256 list; upload_20261114/<V>_model_patch/), then test as for p, compare against p's box test, and save. The compare uses a 1e-6 relative tolerance on CV/HEX because GPU index_add_ is not deterministic. The p2 box script demands exact equality, so its compare line can flag 1e-9 noise as a difference; p2 is left untouched, so read the magnitudes there. An optional archive step builds the full archive (option a). Laptop: rebuild_model_archive_20261114.py (Python 3.8+ standard library) checks the old archive's sha256 (fff3ec09...) and the new file's sha256, then makes one streaming pass old to new without extracting to disk. It then reads the new archive back and requires its per-file list (sha256, size, path; regular files only, world-readable, no '._' files) to equal the box-tested tree's list line for line before renaming .part. Tested on a GNU-tar archive made with tier p's tar options (long names included), on Linux Python 3.12 and on this Mac's /usr/bin/python3 3.9. Negative tests pass: a wrong base archive and a content mismatch are both refused, with .part kept and not renamed.

All 324 differ (largest |difference| 0.303). The only container differences are 10 new config keys from the newer runner (row_weight, window*, appear, shading, batch, clip, target_w). fp16 copy: lane_cellroute_20261109/deploy_fp16/<same path>, 606,531,329 B (old 606,531,073), sha256 aa78c13721f27f25266e739ceeeb4ecb0e1bd4e7b29c9925377a50d797c0db03, written by convert_fp16.one() (the 11-11 rule) and bit-exact. Finding for the CD lane: the checkpoint's stored log_mean / log_std are [7.92014, -0.98154, NaN] / [0.18783, 0.18944, NaN]; the HEX channel is NaN. Cause, bb_runner_full9000_20261113.py (full9000b): logy is NaN for the two HEX-zero rows, and training uses np.nanmean / np.nanstd (line 391, finite), but final.pt and epoch_XX.pt store logy.mean(0) / logy.std(0) (lines 503 / 509), which is NaN in that column. CD and CV have no NaN, so their stored stats are the ones training used. Effect on p3: none. author: coordinator
text: PI question: can the scalar adjustments hurt on the real test? Sensitivity of the p3 strict OOF CD (6.1608, 8,954 rows; reads/cd_tier_t1d_v46_p3_20261114.npz) to an extra change applied to the final prediction. (1) Level, extra multiplier: 0.995 / 1.005 cost +0.015 / +0.018; 0.99 / 1.01 cost +0.063 / +0.069; 0.98 / 1.02 cost +0.259 / +0.266; 0.97 / 1.03 cost +0.580 / +0.579. The shipped level is at the optimum for every subset: best extra multiplier 0.9999 (all rows), 1.0002 (without the 11 rows above 100 % APE), 1.0004 (old-format), 0.9995 (new-format). (2) Spread, extra stretch h around mu = ln 2745 (h = 1 as shipped, g = 1.075): 0.99 +0.0002, 0.97 +0.011, 0.95 +0.035, 0.93 +0.071 (0.93 is about no stretch at all); 1.01 +0.003, 1.03 +0.018, 1.05 +0.045. Over-stretching costs more than under-stretching. (3) Mean log(pred / label) -0.0048 (old-format -0.0081, new-format -0.0014); 53 % of rows predicted below the label. (4) Size of what the post-processing buys: the plain log blend of the four members with the p3 weights and no scalar, mask slot or stretch reads 6.2089; its best single multiplier is 0.9991 and gains 0.0008. So the level scalars themselves are worth almost nothing and move predictions by under 0.1 %; the 0.048 between 6.2089 and 6.1608 comes from the mask slot (about 0.016) and the stretch (about 0.03). Reading: the level scalars are not a risk. The level of the predictions as such is the sensitive quantity (1 % off costs 0.065, 2 % costs 0.26), and it comes from the models, which is why the full-data level check and the 46-frame check were asked for. The stretch is the one post-processing step with a real stake: validated out of fold, never on full-data models or on the real test (submission 1 had no stretch); if the test needed no stretch at all the loss would be about 0.07, if it is off by 3 % about 0.011-0.018. Submission 1's realised CD (6.250 against OOF 6.312) shows no level problem for its full-data models with OOF-fitted scalars.
value: level +/-1 % costs 0.065, +/-2 % costs 0.26; stretch off by 3 % costs 0.011-0.018; level scalars themselves worth 0.0008

author: cd-lane
text: Full-data build checks (coordinator 10:52 message, sent about 10:31), inference only on GPU 3 next to s47 f2. Members were read with the deploy package's own code (package_20261114/p3 .../inference/members.py: CLAHE + percentile preprocessing of the raw frame, four-flip TTA) from img_full_raw9000.dat. Outputs: reads/fulldata_check_20261114.json and fulldata_check2_20261114.json. Conclusion: no CD gap on the 46 unseen frames. The HEX / CV offsets there belong to the frames themselves (the fold models show them too). The new 2e-5 full-data ViT-L s46 sits -1.3 % below the old full-data s46 in CD level, about 3x what the fold pairs show; on the p3 OOF that is worth about +0.002 CD. Found a bug: the 9,000-row runner saves NaN HEX target statistics. PART 1, the 46 frames dropped by the ID match (rows 8954-8999, all three labels positive, never seen by the 8,952-row full-data fits). n = 46, so only a gross gap (about 2 MAPE points, about 2.5 % in level) would show. MAPE on the 46 vs the member's five-fold OOF, then the mean log residual on the 46 (SE) vs OOF. CD: recipe A seed mean 5.23 vs 6.38, -0.40 % (1.15) vs +0.49; recipe A s46 / s47 5.17 / 5.32 vs 6.44 / 6.37; DINOv3-B s46b e16-20 6.13 vs 6.57, -2.60 % (2.30) vs -0.15; ViT-L s46 / s47 6.24 / 6.27 vs 6.50 / 6.47; ViT-L seed mean 6.20 vs 6.43, -2.04 % (1.94) vs -0.15. CV: recipe A 10.64 vs 10.13, +2.53 % (2.05) vs -1.04; DINOv3 10.05 vs 10.44, +3.21 % (1.76); ViT-L 10.36 vs 10.38, +3.49 % (1.82). HEX: recipe A 12.66 vs 10.25, -5.74 % (2.50) vs -0.08; DINOv3 12.98 vs 10.47, -5.88 % (2.46); ViT-L 12.75 vs 10.47, -6.46 % (2.41). HEX is about 2.4 points worse and about 6 % low on these frames, but the fold models (which never saw them either) show the same: ViT-L s46 fold 0 / 4 HEX -5.0 / -6.1 %, CV +2.7 / +3.4 %, CD -2.0 / -2.5 % (CD MAPE 5.34 / 5.81); recipe A s46 fold 0 / 4 HEX -7.1 / -5.8 %, CV +3.4 / +2.6 %, CD -0.3 / +0.9 %. So this is a property of the 46 frames (the alias-recovered IDs, mostly 2019 'xxxx-xxxx XXCN' spellings), not of the full-data builds. The tier-p stack on these rows was not computed: P1 and the mask-slot features do not exist for them in the CD lane files, and P1's crop members were trained on 8,998 rows, so they have seen these frames. PART 2, level of the new full-data ViT-L s46 (2e-5, 9,000 rows) vs the plain full-data s46 (8,952 rows), four-flip TTA. On 1,000 evenly spaced training rows (both trained on them): CD mean log ratio -1.29 % (SD 3.05), slope of new on old 1.049; CV +0.85 % (SD 3.39), slope 0.973; HEX not computable (see the bug below). On the 46 frames: CD +0.68 % (SD 10.2, slope 0.61); only the new build trained on them. The fold pairs read the same way, on their own training rows: fold 0 -0.40 % (SD 2.72, slope 1.029), fold 4 +0.36 % (SD 2.22, slope 0.976). On their OOF rows: -0.45 to +0.43 % per fold, pooled +0.09 %; on the 46 frames -0.12 / +0.65 %. So the full-data pair's CD level gap (-1.3 %) is about 3x the largest fold pair's. Causes that differ for full data: 9,000 vs 8,952 rows, a different data order, and a single run each; target statistics differ by only 0.04 % in log mean. Effect, if the deployed s46 member sits 1.3 % low against what the fold-fitted p3 constants assume: p3 output x0.9979 (V weight 0.30 x the s46 half x stretch g 1.075). On the p3 OOF that is +0.0024 CD; with only the excess over the fold pairs (-0.9 %) it is +0.0011. p3's gain over p2 is -0.0115. Whether to accept it or rescale is for the coordinator / PI. BUG: bb_runner_full9000 trains with HEX statistics over positive labels (nanmean / nanstd) but saves log_mean / log_std with mean / std, so the saved HEX value is NaN. This affects vitlfu_elr2e5_f99_s46 (p3's V file), fu2_elr2e5_f99_s46 (DINOv3), and the s47 full-data build now training (same runner). CD / CV values are correct: CD 7.920138 / 0.18783 vs the old build's 7.920578 / 0.18697. The CD use in p3 is unaffected, but any reader of HEX (or any check that all three outputs are finite) gets NaN. I can write corrected copies with the exact training values (nanmean / nanstd of log HEX over the 9,000 rows), as new files, if the deploy lane needs them. PART 3, how a full-data build differs from the fold runs it stands for. Rows: folds train on four folds (about 7,160) and are read on the fifth; old full-data (recipe A, DINOv3 s46b, plain ViT-L s46 / s47) 8,952 = the old 8,954 minus the two HEX-zero rows (fulldata_regression_split); new 2e-5 builds 9,000 = 8,954 + the 46 frames, with the two HEX-zero rows trained on CD / CV only. SSL init: folds use their own fold SSL; full data uses the full-data SSL (ViT-L arms/vitl16_f99_s46/ssl for s46 and s47, plain and 2e-5 alike; DINOv3 arms/dinov3_b16_f99_s46/ssl; recipe A ssl5_s1003 on all data). Updates and schedule: same epochs (ViT-L 12 with schedule 10; DINOv3 and recipe A 20 with schedule 10). Updates per epoch are ceil(rows / 16), so full data gets about 25 % more updates (560-563 vs about 448 per epoch), with the LR schedule per epoch and so stretched over the extra steps; old vs new full data 560 vs 563. Checkpoint and track: same (raw-track final.pt for ViT-L; epoch_16..20 for DINOv3, the bb runners saving epoch 20 as final.pt; epoch_20.pt for recipe A; no EMA / SWA track read; terminal epoch, no selection; the full-data runs have only a 256-row in-sample monitor). Target statistics: per run over its own training rows (fold, 8,952, or 9,000 positive labels per column); the NaN HEX save in the 9,000-row runner as above. Loss masking: same on all-positive rows; the new builds use masked_loss, whose value is identical there, and the HEX term is zero on the two HEX-zero rows. Runner file: plain ViT-L folds 1-3 and plain full data used lane_cd bb_runner_cd_20261108.py; plain folds 0 / 4 and the 2e-5 fold arms used lane_backbone bb_runner_20261108.py; the new full data uses bb_runner_full9000_20261113.py, a sweep copy of bb_runner_20261108. All share the fine-tune path; the differences are optional switches that are off by default, fold -1 support and zero-label validation handling. All checkpoints load strictly into the deploy package's ViT-L net (today's reads). Images and preprocessing: same loader (CLAHE + 1-99 % scaling, H / V flips); the first 8,954 frames of the 9,000-frame memmap are byte-identical to the old file. Data order is drawn from (seed, epoch, index), so the 9,000-row order differs from the 8,952-row one at the same seed.

text: Hard-image probe launched per the coordinator's 13:27 message, at 13:29:10 EST (pod 18:29:10Z): ViT-L s46 encoder LR 2e-5, fold 0 on GPU 1 and fold 4 on GPU 3, alone on their cards. Commands are exactly the sweep_vitl_elr2e5_f{0,4}_s46 ones (bb_runner_20261108, the same SSL inits, 12 epochs, schedule 10, micro 8, workers 2, EMA 0.999 / 0.9995 on f0 and 0.998 / 0.999 on f4, SWA from 6, keep 8-12, --tta-final, seed 46), plus --row-weight. Roots arms/sweep_vitl_elr2e5_hard2_f{0,4}_s46; launcher source/launch_hard2_20261114.sh. Weight path: --row-weight is a LOSS weight, not a sampling weight. Each row's recipe loss is multiplied by its weight and divided by the mean training weight, so the top decile weighs 1.818 and the rest 0.909; every row is still seen once per epoch. Used as it is, as allowed. Weights (source/make_hard2_weights_20261114.py -> data/rowweight_hard2_f{0,4}_20261114.npz): SD over the four tier-p strict OOF member logs (P1_in, A_in, D, V of reads/cd_tier_t1_20261112.npz; no labels), top decile of each fold's training rows = 2. That is 717 rows per fold, SD threshold 0.0365 vs a median of 0.0163; 177 / 181 validation rows of folds 0 / 4 are above the same threshold. The rows match the runner's split files exactly. Caveat on 'held-out only': each training row's OOF prediction comes from fold models trained on the other four folds, which include the probe fold's own validation rows. The weights are therefore only second-order independent of the probe fold's labels; I do not expect it to matter at weight 2. Reads (source/cd_hard2_read_20261114.py, self-test running): reference = the 2e-5 arm of the same fold in the same form; p3's members for the kept-constants stack (D = s46b alone, V = 2e-5 s46 + plain s47). Member CD / CV / HEX, member CD on the fold's top-disagreement decile and on the rest, the kept-constants stack, and the repeated 10-fold on folds 0 + 4 rows (in the final form, the reference in V's half is p3). Expected (alone on a card, about 9-10 min per epoch): interim at epochs 8-10 single view about 15:10 EST; final (final.pt TTA) read about 15:50 EST. Nothing is expanded automatically; the reads are posted for the PI to decide.

author: cd-lane
text: Answer to the coordinator's 15:15 question on P1, from the run configs (experiments/deploy_review_20260905/staged/model/candidate5.json and the training sources in deploy_review_20260905/source/code) and the ledger. (1) P1 = the mean of five members on the cpsam_v2 (Cellpose-SAM) encoder over the native 512 x 512 central crop (img_native_512.dat): seed42, seed77, seed2026 (train_final_candidate.py: one crop, mean pool), metric35 and predbag2_35 (train_deploy_methods.py; metric35 mixed-MAPE objective with one crop, predbag2_35 log-L1 with two crops). All five use AdamW with encoder LR 1e-5, head LR 1e-3, weight decay 1e-4, batch 48. The OOF schedule is 35 epochs x 149 updates (cosine, floor 0.05, warmup 200) for the method recipes; the seed members run 25 epochs. The deployed builds stop at a frozen update count, the median of the five OOF best counts (metric35 4,470; predbag2_35 3,874; per seed for the seed members). (2) No P1 encoder-LR arm is in the ledger; the only CD-lane LR entries are recipe A (1e-5 CD-only, O-CDTRAIN-1E5-F04; 2e-5 tonight), DINOv3-B and ViT-L. The September curriculum HPO (experiments/curriculum_hpo, run_curriculum_hpo.py) varied the self-supervised JEPA curriculum LRs (low_lr: external 1e-5 / CLEAR 5e-6; high_lr: 3e-5 / 2e-5) for a different representation; that is not P1's supervised fine-tune. Its planned stage 3 (eight encoder / head LR combinations) has no result file I could find, so I cannot say it ran. (3) Cost from the September full-data logs (deploy_methods_20260905/runs/*/progress.json, alone on an H200 then): metric35 4,470 updates in 6,231 s (1.4 s / update), predbag2_35 3,874 updates in 11,632 s (3.0 s / update, two crops). A fold run is the 5,215-update OOF schedule, about 2.0 h for a one-crop member and about 4.4 h for predbag2_35 at those speeds; the CPU-bound pod would be slower. A folds 0 + 4 screen of 2x encoder LR for the whole P1 slot is 5 members x 2 folds = 10 runs (roughly 4 x 2 h + 2 x 4.4 h = about 17 GPU-h, about 4.5-5 h wall on four cards). A one-recipe screen (e.g. the three seed members, the same recipe) is 6 runs at about 2 h, but it changes only part of the five-member mean. (4) The deployed P1 is full-data builds: 8,998 rows (all 9,000 reconciled frames minus the two HEX-zero rows), the five staged .pt files. In the stack it enters through its five-fold OOF (candidate5.json: global scale fitted to historically reused five-fold OOF, not independent validation). An expansion after a two-fold screen would be 5 members x (3 more folds + 1 full-data build) = 20 more runs. Also: the four-fold 3e-5 read (cd_lr3e5_read4_20261114.py) passed its self-test (arm = reference: 0 everywhere; reference = p3b on folds 0 / 1 / 2 / 4, stacks 6.0175 / 6.1025 / 5.8024 / 6.3008).
